title: Legacy behavior emulation proxy for OpenAI ChatCompletions (deterministic tool-call & streaming reconciliation)
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Purpose: implement a lightweight 'behavior emulation' proxy that maps OpenAI Chat Completions (oa-cc) requests and streaming responses to Redwood's canonical request/response envelopes while preserving subtle legacy semantics relied on by customers. Scope includes: deterministic tool/function call mapping, robust streaming delta reconciliation, error and finish_reason translation, role/system message handling, idempotency alignment, and instrumentation for regressions.

Background: customers running legacy clients expect the OpenAI ChatCompletions contract (including streaming deltas and the function_call/arguments evolution over stream chunks). Redwood's native protocol uses a structured tool-invocation envelope and more deterministic argument typing. Without a compatibility shim, some clients see broken tool calls, double-invocations, or truncated arguments when streaming is proxied through our runtime and optimized batching.

Goals:
- Accurately reconstruct function_call.name and arguments from streaming deltas even when arguments are split across token boundaries.
- Guarantee idempotent mapping so retries or hedged requests do not cause duplicate external tool executions.
- Maintain OpenAI finish_reason equivalence mapping (stop, length, function_call) into Redwood outcomes and ensure downstream rollbacks/fallbacks work.
- Translate OpenAI's event stream framing (SSE / NDJSON) into our HTTP/2 framed streaming without losing partial-data semantics.
- Provide telemetry metric set for troubleshooting regressions: reassembly-failures, partial-tool-args, mapped-fallbacks, duplicate-tool-invokes.

Design considerations and constraints:
- Partial-delta aggregation: stream chunks may provide function_call field incrementally (delta.function_call.name, delta.function_call.arguments). We must maintain a per-session incremental buffer keyed by conversation_id + message_id with sequence guards to detect missing chunks. Buffers must be bounded (configurable max_bytes) to avoid OOM on malicious streams.
- Tokenization differences: OpenAI token boundaries vs Redwood tokenization can split UTF-8 codepoints differently; reassembly must operate at byte-string level and preserve UTF-8 safety.
- Deterministic argument normalization: normalized JSON for arguments (sorted keys, stable number formatting) to allow idempotency checks and enable memoization in caching layer.
- Tool signature mapping: map OpenAI function names to Redwood tool IDs using an explicit mapping table per-tenant; when ambiguous, fall back to 'name' passthrough but emit a warning and metric.
- Backpressure & streaming order: maintain original event ordering; when runtime reorders due to batching, attach sequence stamps and reorder before emitting to client.
- Error semantics: map OpenAI error objects and finish_reasons to Redwood error codes and surface both human-friendly and machine-readable fields in the compatibility response envelope.

Non-goals: full parity for undocumented OpenAI edge cases (we will iterate), converting OpenAI-specific model-side behaviors beyond streaming/tool-call semantics (e.g., hidden server-side reranking).

Operational concerns:
- Attack surface: streaming buffers and per-connection state increase memory pressure. The proxy must evict least-recently-updated buffers and return a clear mapping error when limits hit.
- Performance: minimal added latency (<5ms p50) for non-streaming requests; streaming reassembly should not impact per-token throughput substantially.

Deliverables:
1) Compatibility proxy service (binary) with feature flag per-tenant.
2) End-to-end integration tests including: split-argument streaming, mid-token split, retry-on-idempotency-key, ambiguous-name mapping fallback.
3) Telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds.
4) API docs and deprecation notes for customers encouraged to migrate to Redwood native structured tool calls.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
comments: 2026-02-16 Priya Raman: Initial draft and RFC posted to #runtime-compatibility. Requesting design review from runtime and platform teams.
2026-02-18 Elena Novak: Raised memory guard concerns — suggested configurable max_buffer_bytes per-tenant. Action: Marco to add eviction policy and a clear error code.

2026-02-22 Marco Li: Prototype of incremental reassembly implemented (branch: feat/oa-cc-emulation). Handles delta.function_call.*; unit tests added for incremental args concatenation across three chunks.

2026-02-27 QA: Found failure when function_call.arguments include non-ASCII combining characters split across token boundary. Fix: switch to byte-level buffer with UTF-8 validation before emit. Patch merged.
2026-03-01 Security review: confirmed threat model acceptable with buffer limits and tenant-level quotas. Recommended rate-limiting on reconstructor API. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-05 Marco Li: Updated design to include deterministic argument canonicalization and idempotency key generation (sha256 of normalized args + tool name). Added telemetry events for duplicate detects and fallback mapping.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility proxy accepts standard OpenAI ChatCompletions request payloads and returns responses indistinguishable in shape and streaming semantics from OpenAI for existing clients (when feature flag enabled).
Tool/function calls emitted by streaming responses are reconstructed reliably in >99.9% of synthetic split-argument tests (including mid-codepoint splits) within buffer limits.
Idempotency guaranty: repeated identical requests (same idempotency key) do not cause duplicate external tool invocations; verified by integration test harness against a fake tool endpoint.
Failure modes: when maximum buffer or sequence gap occurs, the proxy returns a documented oa-compatibility error code and a human-readable message; error metrics emitted to telemetry.
Performance: non-streaming request latency overhead <5ms p50; streaming throughput degradation <3% on benchmark workloads (runtime-1.20 test harness).
Logs and metrics: reassembly-failures, duplicate-tool-invokes, ambiguous-name-fallbacks, per-tenant buffer-evictions visible in console dashboards with drilldown to request ids.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary (team accounts) behind feature flag; monitor reassembly-failures and memory usage for 48h.
Phase 2: opt-in customers and migration docs released; support window for 2 weeks.
Phase 3: gradual default-on for legacy API clients with per-tenant opt-out for 30 days; finalize deprecation timeline in parallel.
Rollback: kill compatibility proxy in routing layer and route requests to native handler; emit migration guidance URL to client response headers.
